(1) Pipelines are registered as the stage's materials register (registries_, game thread, during the load); the render thread queues the new ones each frame (render_core.cpp, pipelines_queued_) for low-priority workers. The game's load already ends at one gate, GameSystemSceneController::isReadyToStartScene (the load screen's nerve waits there for the scene's worker): it also asks the host that every pipeline registered so far is made (Pipelines::pending() for the set queued, the workers raised to normal priority while the game waits). The load screen keeps stepping as it does for the scene's own load. (2) A draw whose pipeline is still missing in play (a material registered after the load, a settings change) is skipped for that frame and its job moved to the front of the queue at normal priority, never built on the render thread; Vulkan with pipeline libraries keeps its quick link. A miss is a timeline event and counted (made by draws first stays 0 after a stage's first picture). title: (wrong behaviour, suspected) Android's restart starts the new activity in the `:game` process and kills that same process in the same UI-thread task.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed. GameActivity.restartGame (on the UI thread) calls startActivity(GameActivity, NEW_TASK|CLEAR_TASK) and then Process.killProcess(myPid) at once; startActivity only asks the system, which starts the new GameActivity in the process named :game, and that is the one being killed: whether the new one lands in the dying process or a fresh one depends on timing (P-099's CLEAR_TASK also drops the launcher). Design (the ProcessPhoenix pattern): the game asks the launcher's process (a small exported-false activity or service there, Intent with the restart kind) and ends its own process; the launcher's side waits for the old :game pid to be gone (ActivityManager.getRunningAppProcesses, or the pid file) and then starts GameActivity in the task it belongs to, without CLEAR_TASK (P-099). design gap (T3, T6). On vblanks, the real picture of a step is almost never shown, and every step costs one extra unseen walk.
note: Design (read 11-18, E6a, file F G2 part 1): start_interp_sequence gives a lead only off vblanks (locked = !on_vblanks && rate a multiple of 60); on vblanks lead is 0 and the slots follow the display, so t = 1 falls between refreshes and the real picture's walk is made and never shown (5 to 13 of 2,640 steps shown). The step is phased to the display on every host (Windows: FramePhase in svc_frame_wait aims the step at a vblank; SDL: wait_display_frame), so at refresh = k x 60 within 0.2 % (vblanks_per_slot 1 and rate/60 whole) the sequence takes lead 1/k with its slot clock anchored at the vblank nearest the arrival: slots show t = 1/k .. 1, the last the real picture, and no walk is thrown away. Needs I-013 first (FramePhase measures the step's own work) so the phase holds under in-between pictures. Other rates keep lead 0 until passes name what they read (file F). Proof: real pictures shown, counted as file F section 1A did, at 120 and 240 Hz near every step (today 5 to 13 of 2,640), walks per step k (today k + 1), pace.py animation_within_1ms unchanged.

title: performance (T3). Each in-between picture is a full CPU walk and a full GPU frame.
note: Design (read 11-18, E6b with I-002 and P-156): an in-between picture differs from its list's step picture only in the blended rows (transforms, the camera's view) and in which items a moved bound culls. So each draw pass is recorded once per list, at its first picture (DrawRecorder ops, draw_record.h), with every row read through the rows base (encoder set_rows, walk_.rows_address) as the one patched value; an in-between picture writes its blended rows into a new rows slice and replays the recorded ops with that base: no walk of the items, no material or pipeline lookups. Culling: an item culled at both ends of the pair stays culled (the bound's union over the pair, a test at record time), so a replay never misses one; items culled at one end only are recorded and drawn. Passes whose inputs do not depend on t (2D layers not marked present-time, the frame copy of a step picture) are replayed as recorded. The GPU work stays a full frame (a new picture of moved objects); its cost is P-156's, measured per pass. Proof: the timeline's Walk events (b=1 in-between) on the PC at 240 Hz and the tablet at 120 Hz: render-thread time of an in-between picture before and after; the interpolation tours' pictures the same.

title: wrong behaviour (T4). Interpolation adds about one to two steps of latency, and neither camera nor pointer is sampled at present time.
note: Design (read 11-18, E6a's first change, file F G1): the step-moment arrival and its slow delay tracking are in (render_core.cpp start_interp_sequence); what still costs the step is the gate on the present. The game submits list N at its frame end (host_main.cpp svc_submit_frame, present false) and asks for its present only at frame N+1's start (svc_frame_begun -> submit_frame(true, black), NebulaFrameClock onFrame); the render thread holds the list (interp_list_waiting_) until that chunk comes, about 15 ms later. The only reason to wait is black, and black is set only around a restart (NebulaFrameClock::show: GameSystemObjHolder true, GameSystemRestartProcess false). New: svc_submit_frame marks the list's chunk shown when the frame clock shows a picture and the start is not skipping frames (gBootFast); such a chunk starts its sequence when its walk is done (the arrival its own step moment plus the tracked delay, as now), and the next frame's present only supersedes it when it is black; a chunk not marked waits as today. Changed in play: at a restart the last list before black can be shown for up to a step (the console never showed it). Proof: pace.py at 240 Hz with in-between pictures on, delay_avg_us before and after (file F: 42.4 ms to about 26), the timeline's RenderBegin to first present; pictures and replays the same in fixed-step tests.

title: wrong behaviour (T2, T7). Linux has no display clock.
note: Design (read 11-18): Linux gets the display clock from the presents themselves. The Vulkan renderer already makes its swap chain with present ids and present wait (VK_KHR_present_id2/present_wait2, renderer_vk.cpp), which Mesa and NVIDIA's driver give on X11 and Wayland: a waiter thread waits on each present id and stamps when it completed; the stamps fitted to the mode's period (SDL_GetCurrentDisplayMode, refined by the stamps' median spacing) are the vblank grid display_clock.cpp hands the slots, as the Choreographer's are on Android. Where VK_EXT_present_timing is offered, its present-stage times and refresh duration take that place. No grid (no present wait) keeps today's clock. Proof: Linux at 144 Hz with present-stats: the vblank-steps histogram filled, no two pictures in one refresh over 3000 pictures; a unit test of the fit fed stamps with jitter and a missed refresh.

title: wrong behaviour (T2), suspected. Metal drops a picture when `nextDrawable` waited more than 1.5 ms.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed as a guess where a count is available. renderer_mtl.mm present: with VSync on, a frame whose nextDrawable took more than kDrawableWaitMs (1.5 ms) is not handed over (held_last_, never two frames running), to take one queued picture out of the layer's line. The wait time stands in for the line's length: a wake-up late by scheduling, a display link phase or a ProMotion rate change waits as long with an empty line, and that frame is lost (a visible skip). The renderer already adds a presented handler to every drawable (the pacing recorder). Design: count drawables handed over and not yet presented (up at presentDrawable, down in the presented handler, presentedTime 0 included) and hold a picture back only when that count is 2 or more at the moment the drawable comes; the wait time is no longer read. Proof: Mac run with --diagnostics timeline, a test hook that delays the render thread by 2 ms every 30th frame: no picture held before the count says the line is full (pictures_held_ 0), the start's queued pictures still drained (latency at hand-over as now).

note: Design (read 11-18, E6a; renderer_common.h next_variable_refresh, renderer_d3d12.cpp refresh_display_rate): variable refresh is not inferred from the vblank thread's rate (that rate follows the presents once it is on, and near the mode rate it never falls under 0.8 of it). It is asked of the system where it answers (Vulkan VK_EXT_present_timing / display timing where present; Apple: the display link's minimum and maximum rates, ProMotion) and proved from the presents everywhere: with presents held at a rate between the mode and half of it (variable_refresh_cap), a fixed-rate display shows each picture for whole mode periods (DXGI frame statistics: PresentRefreshCount steps of 1 and 2), a variable one for the presents' own interval (steps follow the presents, SyncQPCTime intervals equal the present intervals). The test runs on the frame statistics already read (DisplayStats events), at the first seconds after a display change, and its answer holds until the next change. When variable: the slots follow the arrival clock at the cap (the present pacer's QPC clock), never the vblank thread's grid, so the slot clock and the display no longer feed each other; VSync stays on with tearing allowed above the range. The same on D3D11 and Vulkan (their callers of next_variable_refresh). design gap (T6), suspected. Two governors act on the same GPU time without knowing of each other.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed in code. Dynamic resolution (renderer_d3d12.cpp, once per scene picture) aims the scene pictures' GPU time at resolution_budget_ms(present_frame_rate(cap, VSync, refresh)), the display's rate; the interpolation governor (render_core.cpp interp_gpu_governor) picks k generated pictures a step from interpolation_gpu_cost_ms against 0.9 of a step and runs the slot clock at 60 x (k + 1). Neither reads the other: with k capped below the display's rate the pictures come at 60 x (k + 1) while dynamic resolution budgets 1/refresh, so it lowers the resolution further than the rate in use needs; the cheaper pictures then let the interpolation governor raise k after 2 s, which tightens the real budget again, a slow loop between the two (dynamic resolution steps up after 60 pictures, k after 120 sequences). Design: one controller owns both (k, sixteenths) against one budget, the slot period in use: the display's rate is filled first (k up to refresh/60 - 1) at no less than the resolution floor, then resolution rises in the time left; over budget, resolution falls to the floor before k falls. Proof: a unit test of the controller fed measured costs (a heavy scene at 144 Hz: one stable (k, sixteenths), no alternation over 3000 pictures); then the run the audit asks for, [dynres] and [interp-stats] gpu-generated-cap on a heavy galaxy at 144 Hz.

note: Read 11-18: the timeline is Windows only in code, not just in use: frame_timeline.h's now() returns 0 and initialize()/dump() are empty outside _WIN32, so --diagnostics timeline on Android, Linux or Mac writes nothing (luma_test_android.py asks for it anyway). Design: the POSIX side with clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) in nanoseconds (the header's frequency field says 1e9, so tools/perf/timeline_digest.py is unchanged), gettid, and a plain file write at the orderly exit the host already calls; Apple the same with mach_absolute_time and its timebase. It comes first in E3 (the tablet trace needs it). Test: a unit test in tests/unit (Linux runs it) that records, dumps and reads back the header and records. title: wrong behaviour (minor), suspected. FramePhase measures the wrong work under interpolation.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed, as the audit (E) says. host_main.cpp next_frame_start takes a step's work as g_last_present_ns minus the previous step's start; RenderCore stamps g_last_present_ns only for a real picture (render_core.cpp, note_picture_shown when `real`). With in-between pictures on, a step's real picture is shown about two steps after the step, or never (I-002), so work is that arrival delay or 0 (the budget left as it was), and the phase aims at vblank - (delay + 1.5 ms), not at the step's own work. Design: the measure is keyed by the step: the render thread records, for each frame index, when that step's list was taken and its picture rendered (one slot per frame index, written beside the timeline's SubmitEnd and RenderSubmitted), and next_frame_start reads the entry of the step that started at previous_ns, with or without in-between pictures. Proof: a unit test of the measure fed a step rendered at +5 ms whose real picture is shown at +30 ms: work 5 ms (before: 30 ms or 0); and the timeline at 120 Hz with interpolation, StepWaitEnd against VBlank.

title: wrong behaviour (T2), suspected. Game-declared camera cuts come from two places only.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed in code. MotionSignal::cameraCut fires only in CameraViewInterpolator::reduceOscillation when mIsForceCameraChange (setInterpolation(0)) and at CameraAnim cut frames. CameraDirector::isInterpolationOff also counts a camera man that declares its own interpolation off (CameraManEvent::isInterpolationOff, an event camera that snaps): that switch is instant but sends no cut, so the host's heuristic (60 degrees, or 1500 units and 6x the last move) decides, and a snap to a near angle is blended for one step. FrameList writes camera_epoch (sCuts) and nothing reads it: the host reads NEBULA_FRAME_CAMERA_CUT. Design: the cut is sent where the game decides a camera does not interpolate: CameraDirector::switchAntiOscillation when isInterpolationOff() (both causes), CameraAnim's cut frames as now, and the director's restart paths after a warp or a scene start; camera_epoch leaves the frame list (one signal, the flag). Proof: the tour's present-stats with in-between pictures on: game-cuts against camera-cuts at pipes, doors and event cameras (every heuristic cut there also a game cut), generated pictures at a door with no blend, and the step-hash replay the same (the signal is not game state).

title: (console-era remnant, audio sync): the step learns that a music stream ended from the audio device. The audio thread counts a stream's finishes as the device takes its samples (StreamPlayer.hpp:26-28); StreamSound::finished compares that count on the game thread (StreamSound.cpp:122-124), tryDie_ kills the sound on it (:263-266), the handle detaches, and AudBgm::isStopping answers true (AudBgm.hpp:76-82), which MR::isPlayingStageBgm and its family read (SoundUtil.cpp:378-440; git grep -c -E 'MR::is(Playing|Stage)[A-Za-z]*(Bgm|BGM)' in native/petari/src: 32 lines). So the step on which a non-looping music ends follows the device's buffer and latency, and the ticks dropped after a stall (SoundEngine.cpp:151-160): the console's sound and picture ran from one clock.
note: Found by the readall harness's sound-area reports (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. The play position itself (the beat) is read only by the audio thread's sequence clock (TempoAdjuster::sequenceSeconds, RhythmSystem.cpp:100-110, set at :187): no step reads it. Replay: the same on every device afterwards, not the same as each device's run today (a question for the owner only if today's runs must be matched).

title: (console-era remnant, rumble and battery): rumble runs through a per-channel registry made for the console's motor callback (InputRumble::sInstanceForCallback, InputRumble.cpp:10, :62-67, :81-88; switched between a pad's game and menu rumble at GameSystemFunction.cpp:153-188). Each pad's two InputRumble objects both call update every step (PlayerInput.cpp:37-38), and each update advances the registered one (InputRumble.cpp:116-125), so the registered rumble's channels step twice a step (mStep++ at :51) and the other never steps. The battery is copied from the device record at connect and then every 300 seconds of steps (InputInfoChecker.cpp:7, :18-22, :29-39), the interval of the console's info request.
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/System report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. To check before the fix: whether the disc's InputRumble::update also advanced the registered instance from both objects (then the patterns' double rate is as made and is kept, written as the pattern's own rate). package: E8 console limits and gameplay rules

BasaBasa goes home after cClipResetSteps out of view and away from the player (tryClippingAndResetPos, BasaBasa.cpp:658-685, isJudgedToClipFrustum at :664); Gesso goes home after 5 s out of view or past 10,000 units (clipAndInitPos, Gesso.cpp:417-433); Petari jumps out only while on screen (tryShiftJumpOut, calcScreenPosition, Petari.cpp:458-466). Two rules have clipping as their only end or sleep: an escaping BombBird ends only when it becomes clipped (BombBird.cpp:126-132), a Kameck sleeps only from startClipped (Kameck.cpp:166-169). And actors that switch off their own work by distance from the player, the same on every screen: Kuribo past 3000 units (Kuribo.cpp:469-487), PackunPetit past 5000 with sensors, animation and shadow off (PackunPetit.cpp:89-99, :489-496), and by the report Karikari, KoteBug, Poihana, TakoHei, Metbo and Begoman.

Same questions.

package: E8 console limits and gameplay rules
title: (behaviour by the screen's size; question for the owner): the pointer's screen position is scaled by MR::getScreenWidth (StarPointerController.cpp:68), which is the display's width when it is wide (ScreenUtil.cpp:88-93), and its velocity is the difference of two positions (:96-99); rules compare that velocity with fixed numbers: a fireball reflects when it is over 30 (FireBall.cpp:225-228), and by the report FireBubble over 10, StringSpider at 20, Karikari's flick and release. title: (crash or wrong state, map objects): the spider web binds an actor into hang info mNumHangInfos with no bound against its 64 (SpiderThread::startActorBind, SpiderThread.cpp:160, made at :90-93, the size 8 x 8 at :28, :36); findNearestPointPos leaves the point null when no part is within 1800 units (:349-370, :30) and SpiderCoin then reads it (SpiderCoin.cpp:94-99); findHangInfo answers slot 0 for an actor not bound (:372-380) and the apart message then counts below zero (:302-310). An electric rail's type is placement arg 3 cast unchecked (ElectricRail.cpp:217-219) and indexes four models (ElectricRailHolder.cpp:170-172, :204). A power star's appear point is the nearest other member of a group stars and points both join (PowerStar.cpp:391, PowerStarAppearPoint.cpp:14), cast to an appear point (PowerStar.cpp:488-509) and its camera info read at that class's layout (:519-525): a second star in the group is read as a point. OceanWaveFloater takes its parameters by object name and uses the null of a name not in its two rows (OceanWaveFloater.cpp:36-45, :54). JetTurtle compares mLastGravity before any write (JetTurtle.cpp:567-571; not set in the constructor, :39). SnowFloorTile writes depths at (y << shift) + x and reads them at y * size + x (SnowFloorTile.cpp:72, :353 against :303, :374, :403-410), the same only when the size is a power of two; the size is 32 x the tile's scale (:45-53).

Fix: the hang infos grow; no bind without a point; the apart message only for a bound actor; the rail type checked at init (refused with a message); appear points told by class; an unknown floater name refused at init; mLastGravity zeroed (the first throw blends as the game's does in practice); one index form. Replay identical for the disc's content (SnowFloorTile where its sizes are powers of two).

title: (hitch, map objects): actors made inside a step when a pool is empty: CoinHolder makes 32 coins and runs their after-placement init in the step that asks (takeDeadCoin, CoinHolder.cpp:131-152), and by the report the air bubble, big bubble, star piece and pressure bullet pools the same way. Collision built by a dynamic object is one octree leaf holding every prism (DynamicCollisionObj::createCollision, DynamicCollisionObj.cpp:146-170), so every query against it tests every triangle.
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/MapObj report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Modern form: pools made at load to the scene's count (and grown off the step when a mod's scene asks more); a dynamic collision object a BVH refitted when its vertices move. Replay identical (query order kept).

title: (render choices in the game step): PunchBox recomputes its shadow once every 128 steps (PunchBox.cpp:115-128), work spread for the console's CPU. Not a render choice, on reading: the level-of-detail control a map object updates in the step (MapObjActor.cpp:324-326, :432-434; createLodCtrlPlanet, LiveActorUtil.cpp:2563-2568) follows the view cubes the player stands in (ViewGroupCtrl.cpp:60-83, LodCtrl.cpp:80-102), a rule of the level's content the same on every screen, and a hidden model turns off its parts' sensors (PartsModel.cpp:66-72): it stays in the step.
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/MapObj report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Modern form: the shadow recomputed on change; the cubes' level stays a step rule and the renderer draws the model it names. Replay identical. 11-18 (the harness's Boss report, checked at 241395b49): also a part that hides its model by a frustum test in the step (TripodBossFixPartsBase.cpp:102-106) and the shark's flat shadows switched by the one camera's direction in calcAnim (SkeletalFishBoss.cpp:255-271). 11-18 (the harness's Ride report, checked at 241395b49): the bubble picks its surface's subdivision 1 to 6 from its projected radius and tessellates in calcAnim (BigBubble.cpp:188-208).

title: (determinism, the game's random stream advanced by drawing): MR::getRandom is the game's one stream (MathUtil.cpp:18-23, the scene's mRandom), and Mario's draw and view code draws from it: the spin ring takes 130 numbers in each const drawSpinEffect (MarioActorSpecialDraw.cpp:547-590, from the draw at MarioActorDraw.cpp:786), the wall-shade noise 64 in each updateRandomTexture (MarioActorSpecialDraw.cpp:355-383, from calcViewWallShadowModel, MarioActorShadow.cpp:256), the dark mask 2 in each updateDarkMask while the mask is on (:632-644, twice from calcViewAndEntry, MarioActorDraw.cpp:474-475). GameSystem::frameLoop draws once a frame while a mod's time rate or a cutscene skip runs more steps (GameSystem.cpp:182-205), so every later random number in the game depends on how many frames were drawn, not only on the steps.
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/Player report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Modern form: the draw-side noise from its own generator seeded from the step (or made in the shader from a seed and the timer); the step's stream advanced only by the step. Replay: changes once for every run that shows the spin ring, the wall shade or the dark mask (a question for the owner); or, kept identical for runs of one step a frame, the same calls moved to the end of the step (the skip's and a time rate's runs then change).

title: (hang or memory, the player): Mario::delTask never moves its cursor, so removing a task that is not first or second in the ring spins for ever (MarioTask.cpp:37-58); pushTask writes past its 11 slots when all are taken (:135-143); the ghost's lead-in skip loops for ever when the recording ends while the fourth track's weight is above 0.9, since receiveGhostFrame then returns 0 and nothing changes (GhostPlayer.cpp:250-265, :607-613); the shadow's mode 3 reads the reference model's matrix before its null check (MarioShadow.cpp:376-381); the eyelid set-up writes the bee's and hopper's texture headers into a table sized for Mario's model (MarioActorDraw.cpp:592-642); the miss sequences' addEvent calls have no bound (PlayerEvent.cpp:74-102; today's sequences fit); Mario's effects are registered under name + materialIndex, a pointer 0 to 6 bytes into a UTF-8 name (MarioEffect.cpp:478, :484, :493-499, :507, :511), so the keys start inside a character and are distinct only by chance.
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/Player report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Fix: the cursor advances; the task slots grow (or a full table refused with a message); the skip loop ends with the recording; the null check first; the table sized for the largest model; the event counts checked; effects registered under (entry, material). Replay identical.

title: (crash, hang or wrong state, NPCs): the take-out-star event is registered for every Caretaker with a message, every Toad and every Luigi (CareTaker.cpp:84-87, Kinopio.cpp:103, LuigiNPC.cpp:55-57) while the star exists only in star mode (CareTaker.cpp:108, Kinopio.cpp:206-207, LuigiNPC.cpp:158-160); event 0 on another one calls through null (Kinopio.cpp:62, LuigiNPC.cpp:47 set it null) or through an unset pointer (the Caretaker's constructor never sets mTakeOutStar). DemoRabbit bends its run toward up until no collision lies 200 units ahead and loops for ever when collision lies straight up (DemoRabbit.cpp:162-166). PowerStarEventKeeper makes a star's bit as 1 << (scenarioNo - 1) in an s32 (PowerStarEventKeeper.hpp:32-34) and indexes its table, sized to the galaxy's star count (PowerStarEventKeeper.cpp:16), by any id the mask allows (:65-71, :169-175; getStarInfo unbounded, .hpp:28-30). A Rabbit with placement arg 1 outside 0..3 gets no nerve and reads an unset mBehavior (Rabbit.cpp:102-127, :137; the constructor :60 sets none). TrickRabbitSnowCollect uses its third child rabbit with no check that the placement has three (TrickRabbitSnowCollect.cpp:52, :63-64, :331-336). The talk text former walks a pane it does not check for null (TalkTextFormer.cpp:61-62), though its finder allows one (:20-26). RunawayRabbitCollect asks isValidSwitchA and drops the answer, so its switch A is never turned on when every rabbit is caught (RunawayRabbitCollect.cpp:282-283; the full form at RunawayTico.cpp:146-147).
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/NPC report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Fix: the event registered only with a star (or null-checked), the members set in the constructors; the bend loop bounded; star ids checked against the count; a bad arg 1 refused at init with a message; the children counted at init; the pane checked. note: Found by the readall harness's Game/Boss report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Fix: an unknown name refused at init with a message. package: E8 console limits and gameplay rules

Translucent model draws are keyed by depth under the one global view (ItemBuffer::entryZSort, Model.cpp:317-331, ModelSys::mViewMtx), so the step's camera fixes their order for every picture drawn from it; material entries are merged by scanning every entry already in the buffer (Model.cpp:306-311), quadratic per fill. Modern form: each view a whole record (camera, projection, viewport, scissor) named by id when a pass begins, nothing latched or read back; each model enters its meshes once and the planner sorts translucent draws per view at the picture's camera (E4); entries merged through a map keyed by image and material. package: E8 console limits and gameplay rules

title: (replay, the wall clock decides step counts): the stage's load after the star is chosen runs in slices of 4 ms of wall time (GameScene::initAfterScenarioChosen, GameScene.cpp:165-217; the placement's own deadline, StageDataHolder.cpp:168 and PlacementInfoOrdered.cpp:139), resumed once a frame from the star select's nerves (ScenarioSelectScene.cpp:277, :312, :320, through GameSystemSceneController.cpp:151-163), and each of those frames runs the scene's update and the star select's (GameSystemSceneController.cpp:240-251, :480-487). A skipped cutscene runs extra steps in a frame while 9 ms of wall time last (NebulaCutsceneSkip.cpp:46-47, tryExtraStep :384-399, GameSystem.cpp:199-202). So how many frames lie between the choice and play, and how many steps a skip runs in each frame, follow the computer's speed; the game's random stream is seeded before the star select (GameSystemSceneController.cpp:127), so a draw in those frames would move it by machine. The placement's id sets are found by a scan of every set per placement (PlacementInfoOrdered.cpp:157-166), quadratic in a level's placements.
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/Demo and Game/Scene reports (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Modern form: the stage loads on a load worker (or in one piece) and no frame steps game state that the stage keeps while it loads; a skip runs a fixed number of steps per frame or runs to its end with the input held; the id sets found through a map. To show with the probe (P-242): the step hash at play's first step on a fast and a slowed machine. Replay: identical once the load and the skip no longer read the clock.

title: (particles move by how often they are drawn): the direction draws rebuild and store the particle's base axis (ParticleDraw.cpp:586-593, :637-638, :839-840, :924-925, :976-977), and the particle's step reads it: a child made in calc starts on its parent's axis (ParticleCore.cpp:179, made from :252-254), and GravityDust's particle callback, run from calc (ParticleCore.cpp:240-242, :289-291), takes the axis as its speed's direction and writes it back (GravityDust.cpp:25, :55). Several draws in one step give the same axis up to rounding (the rebuilt axis is already square to the direction), but steps run with no draw (extra world steps, GameSystem.cpp:193-197; a skipped cutscene's, :199-202) skip the rebuild, and a frame drawn twice rounds twice.
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/Particle report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. The draw already knows a particle's first draw of a frame (sFresh, ParticleDraw.cpp:41, :147) but does not guard these writes. Fix: the axis rebuilt in the particle's step (calc, once a step, as the console's one draw a step did) and the draw only reads it. Replay: the console's at one draw a step, now on every rate.

title: (crash and wrong behaviour, rides): a rush cancel clears the manta's rider and leaves it in RideFree (SurfRay.cpp:475-478), whose step still reads player 1's spin (updateRideFree :585, tryJumpOrFall :935-961), so a spin anywhere while the free manta is bound to ground or in water sends it to RideJump or RideJumpHigh, which play the player's surf jump (:229, :241) and start a sound on the null rider (:231, :243), read through at once by MR::startSound (SoundUtil.cpp:118-119). A pole's top joint is set only for Pole and PoleSquare (Pole.cpp:141-147), but appear() sends any pole to DemoAppear (:190-193), which writes the joint through it (:207, :214; updateTopPos :729-740), so a TreeCube or model-less pole a demo makes appear writes through null.

Fix: the manta leaves the ride nerves on a cancel (to Wait, or a free nerve that reads no player); updateTopPos writes the joint only where it was found. title: (memory and order, the scene's run lists): NameObjCategoryList::execute walks a category with a NameObj** cursor and reads end() again on each pass, so that a call may add or remove (NameObjCategoryList.cpp:22-32); but add pushes onto an MR::Vector whose storage grow() moves to a new block when full (:47-51; Array.hpp:111-119, :399-402), leaving the cursor in the old block, and remove moves the last object into the removed place (:53-71), so a removal at or before the cursor skips that object for the pass. The game's own connects and disconnects are requests run between the lists' runs (SceneExecutor.cpp:38-40, :81, reaching NameObjExecuteHolder.cpp:153-196); the immediate path is MR::connectNow (NameObjExecuteHolder.cpp:312-318, :386-387), which LumaUi calls when a mod makes a layout (LumaUi.cpp:671-674), from whatever the mod was running in.
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/NameObj report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Fix: the run iterates by index against the live size, and adds and removes made during a category's run are applied at its end (or connectNow refuses inside a run and queues). Replay: identical for the disc's content (its changes go through the requests); a mod's run gains a defined order.
